soyabeans: Soybeans prefer moderately warm temperatures (17–21 °C) and slightly acidic soils (pH 6.0–7.0). As a legume, soyabeans require relatively little nitrogen, but need adequate phosphorus and potassium. They grow best with moderate rainfall (around 70–90 mm/month).
apple: Apples thrive in temperate climates with temperatures around 18–24 °C. They grow best in slightly acidic soils (pH 5.5–6.3) and require high humidity and rainfall above 100 mm per month. Apples need a moderate amount of nitrogen and a balanced supply of phosphorus and potassium.
banana: Bananas grow well in very warm, humid environments (25–30 °C) with heavy rainfall over 100 mm/month. They prefer slightly acidic soils (pH 5.5–6.5). Bananas have a high demand for potassium and also need sufficient nitrogen.
beans: Beans grow best in moderate temperatures (15–23 °C) and slightly acidic soils (pH 5.5–6.2). They require a medium to high amount of water (60–130 mm/month). As legumes, beans fix nitrogen from the air and mainly need phosphorus and potassium.
coffee: Coffee grows in tropical to subtropical climates with temperatures of 20–27 °C. It prefers slightly acidic soils (pH 5.5–6.8) and requires high rainfall (150 mm or more), but does not tolerate waterlogging. Coffee has a high nitrogen demand due to its perennial nature.
cotton: Cotton prefers warm to hot climates (25–30 °C) and neutral to slightly alkaline soils (pH 6.5–7.5). It does well with moderate rainfall (below 100 mm/month) and is tolerant of dry spells. Cotton has a high nitrogen requirement.
cowpeas: Cowpeas grow well in warm conditions (25–30 °C) and in soils that are neutral to slightly alkaline (pH 7.0–7.2). They need low to moderate rainfall (around 40–60 mm/month) and are drought-tolerant. As legumes, cowpeas require little nitrogen.
grapes: Grapes are adaptable to a wide temperature range (15–25 °C or warmer) and grow in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 5.5–6.5). They do best with moderate rainfall (60–80 mm/month). Grapes need phosphorus and potassium for fruiting, while excessive nitrogen should be avoided.
groundnuts: Groundnuts grow in warm climates (20–30 °C) and usually prefer soils with pH between 6.0 and 7.5, although they can tolerate higher values. Their water needs are moderate (30–70 mm/month). As legumes, they require little nitrogen but need potassium and calcium.
maize: Maize grows best in temperate to warm temperatures (18–25 °C) and slightly acidic soils (pH 5.5–6.8). It needs average rainfall (60–110 mm/month) and has high nitrogen requirements, with moderate needs for phosphorus and potassium.
mango: Mango trees prefer hot climates (30–35 °C) with high rainfall (80–100+ mm/month). They grow in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 5.5–6.5). Mangoes have moderate fertilizer needs and tolerate heat well.
orange: Oranges grow in subtropical regions with temperatures between 20–31 °C. They prefer slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 6.0–7.5) and need high humidity and rainfall above 100 mm/month. Potassium is especially important for good fruit quality.
peas: Peas grow in temperate to warm climates (18–30 °C) and do best in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 5.5–7.0). They often require high rainfall (100 mm or more). As legumes, peas need little nitrogen, but phosphorus and potassium are important.
rice: Rice thrives in warm, wet environments (20–27 °C) and grows in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 5.0–7.5). It needs flooded fields or very high rainfall (often over 180 mm/month). Rice has a high nitrogen requirement.
watermelon: Watermelons prefer warm temperatures (25–30 °C) and slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 6.0–7.0). While they don’t need extreme rainfall, they do require consistent moisture (40–100 mm/month). Watermelons need high potassium and moderate to high nitrogen for healthy fruit growth.
